chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Jamil ibn Durraj, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

The stability of the religion depends on four: a speaking scholar who acts upon his knowledge, a wealthy person who is not stingy with his bounty upon the people of God's religion, a poor person who does not sell his afterlife for his worldly life, and an ignorant person who is not too arrogant to seek knowledge. When the scholar conceals his knowledge, the wealthy person is stingy with his wealth, the poor person sells his afterlife for his worldly life, and the ignorant person becomes too arrogant to seek knowledge, the world will retreat backwards. Do not be deceived by the multitude of mosques and the bodies of people who differ [in appearance/sect]. It was said: O Commander of the Faithful, how should one live in that time? He said: Mix with them outwardly, meaning in appearance, and differ from them inwardly. A person has what he earned and will be resurrected with whom he loves, and await the relief from God, the Exalted.

key_terms.آخِرَتَهُ بِدُنْيَاهُ: Selling the afterlife for the worldly life
key_terms.عَالِمٍ نَاطِقٍ: Speaking scholar (one who acts on knowledge)
key_terms.قَوَامُ الدِّينِ: Stability or pillar of the religion

ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars that strengthen the religion according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the socio-spiritual pillars of religious stability, emphasizing the complementary roles of the scholar, the generous wealthy, the pious poor, and the humble seeker. It introduces the concept of 'khalaṭuhum bi-l-burānīyah' (mixing with them outwardly) as a key strategy for believers during times of decline, ensuring social cohesion while maintaining inner fidelity to faith. The text underscores that individual accountability ('what one has earned') remains intact even amidst societal regression, culminating in the expectation of divine relief (al-Faraj).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-5 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah Al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Jameel ibn Dur’raj, on the authority of Zurarah that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) narrated that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “

There are four issues that will strengthen the religion: outspoken scholars who act according to their knowledge; rich folks who are not stingy in assisting those who adhere to God’s Religion; poor folks who do not outsell their religious beliefs to worldly affairs; and ignorant folks who are not too arrogant to quest for knowledge. Once the knowledgeable ones hide their knowledge, the rich are stingy with their wealth, the poor trade their afterlife in exchange for this world and the ignorant are too arrogant to seek knowledge, the world will start to retreat. At that time you should not be fooled by the increasing number of mosques and the many who go there.” The Imam (MGB) was asked, “O Commander of the Faithful! How should one live at that time?” The Imam (MGB) replied, “Associate with the people superficially. One only gets what he earns and will be resurrected with whatever he likes. Await relief to be sent by the Honorable the Exalted God.”
